correctness.rationale: For each edge, exactly two common neighbors make every open vertex link a disjoint union of cycles; each closed neighborhood has internal minimum degree at least three. If degree is smaller than k, the closed neighborhood violates psi_k; if it equals k, either the link contains a triangle causing an induced K4 or is a union of cycles of length at least four and violates psi_k itself. This proves delta>=k+1 for all k>=4. Euler gives the stated genus bound. The icosahedron is checked exactly for phi0 and psi4 and its uniqueness at order twelve follows by forcing the two pentagonal rings and poles. The triangular torus is six-regular and has two common neighbors per edge; all induced 4- and 5-cycles are excluded by lifting to the planar triangular lattice and applying the triangulated-disk boundary-degree identity. The included checker exhaustively evaluates relevant induced subgraphs for the two small witnesses; these computations are finite certificates, not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The main 2026 source proves only a planar obstruction at local depth six. Its argument, and the underlying 2025 axiomatization, do not state the sharp sphere depth-four/depth-five transition, a twelve-vertex optimal sphere witness, or the toroidal depth-five/depth-six transition with an explicit triangular-torus family. A previously established lower genus bound at depths six and above covers the general quadratic-growth phenomenon, which is not claimed as new; the new implications are the exact low-genus cutoffs and their witnesses, plus the sharpened local degree lemma. Searches of the named index and topical literature did not identify an equivalent combined theorem; this is not a proof of publication priority.

value.rationale: The recent pseudofiniteness result leaves the exact local-axiom depth obstructed by low-genus embedding unresolved. The theorem supplies the sharp first two surface thresholds with constructive attainment, identifies an optimal 12-vertex planar realization, and gives a uniform minimum-degree barrier that translates logical approximation depth into topological complexity. The low-genus cutoff and explicit toroidal family are mathematically motivated structural boundaries rather than arbitrary counts or a mere one-step numerical optimization. The already-known generic quadratic genus growth is deliberately not treated as the new contribution.
